4.meaning: The Especially Merciful: one who actively and continually bestows mercy. From the divine attributes, it stresses mercy as ongoing, effective compassion shown to its recipients. The pattern (faʿīl) is intensive, conveying that this mercy is deep, constant, and abundant.
4.grammar: A definite adjective/name on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun (as a description) or follows a preposition or oath particle.

1.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

2.meaning: He sees you / He watches you — third-person masculine singular present of 'to see', with a second-person masculine singular object; describing Allah's all-encompassing sight of the Prophet.

parts.en: He sees (Form I muḍāriʿ 3rd masculine singular)

2.grammar: yarā is Form I muḍāriʿ third-person masculine singular of the defective root r-ʾ-y (seeing). The suffix -ka is second-person masculine singular object 'you'.

3.meaning: 'Time / moment / period when' — a point or span of time; often used to mean 'at the time that …' or 'when'.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'a time / moment'. The '-a' ending here functions adverbially, giving the sense 'at the time when …', and is also the form taken as the object of a verb. It frequently introduces a clause and behaves like the conjunction 'when'.

4.meaning: You stand / you rise — second-person masculine singular present of 'to stand up or rise'; used for standing in prayer or for arising at night for worship.

parts.en: you stand / rise (Form I muḍāriʿ 2nd masculine singular)

4.grammar: Form I muḍāriʿ second-person masculine singular (ta- prefix, -u indicative). The root q-w-m conveys rising, standing, and establishing oneself — including the standing of prayer.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; establishment

1.meaning: And your movements / and your turning about — conjunction plus the verbal noun of 'to turn or move about', with a second-person masculine singular possessive; referring to all the Prophet's movements.

parts.en: your turning / movements (Form V verbal noun, accusative)

1.grammar: The wa- is conjunctive. taqalluba is the Form V verbal noun (tafaʿʿul pattern: reflexive/intensive of q-l-b), in the accusative (-a ending). The suffix -ka is 2nd masculine singular possessive 'your'.
1.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, to flip; movements, turning about

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

3.meaning: A noun (active participle) meaning 'those who prostrate / the ones bowing down' — people characterized by the act of prostration in worship.
3.grammar: A definite plural active participle ('the ones who prostrate'). The sound masculine-plural ending -īna marks the genitive or accusative case (the form used after prepositions or as an object), as opposed to -ūna used for the subject.
3.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in submission

1.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
1.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

2.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

3.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
3.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

4.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
4.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
1.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

2.meaning: 'I inform you, I give you news of' — a first-person verb meaning to announce or tell someone of something weighty or significant. The doubled middle root letter intensifies it: to convey important tidings.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in an intensive (form II) pattern. The u- prefix signals a first-person singular subject ('I'), the final -u is the indicative ending (a plain statement), and the attached -kum is the object 'you (all)'. So: 'I inform you all.'

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
4.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

5.meaning: They descend / they come down — third-person masculine plural present of 'to descend gradually'; in context referring to the false claim that devils bring down revelation.

parts.en: they descend (Form V muḍāriʿ 3rd masculine plural)

5.grammar: Form V muḍāriʿ (reflexive/intensive descent: coming down oneself) third-person masculine plural (-u indicative). The form implies a repeated or deliberate coming down.
5.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend; Form V: to descend oneself

6.meaning: The satans / devils — the plural of 'shayṭān', a rebellious, malevolent being (from a root sense of being remote from good or burning with rebellion) who tempts and leads astray; with the definite article.
6.grammar: Definite ('al-') broken (internal) plural. The final '-u' ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word is the subject or doer of an action ('the devils ___').
6.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be far/remote (from good); rebellious, devil

1.meaning: They descend / they come down — third-person masculine plural present of 'to descend gradually'; in context referring to the false claim that devils bring down revelation.

parts.en: they descend (Form V muḍāriʿ 3rd masculine plural)

1.grammar: Form V muḍāriʿ (reflexive/intensive descent: coming down oneself) third-person masculine plural (-u indicative). The form implies a repeated or deliberate coming down.
1.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend; Form V: to descend oneself

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
3.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

4.meaning: A great liar / a habitual fabricator — an intensive adjective (faʿʿāl pattern) meaning one who lies excessively and fabricates widely; a shameless deceiver.

parts.en: a great liar / a habitual fabricator (indefinite genitive)

4.grammar: The -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks indefinite genitive (in a construct chain or after a preposition). affāk is the faʿʿāl intensive form: one who constantly produces falsehood and fabrication.
4.root: أ-ف-ك (ā-f-k) — to lie, to fabricate; turning away from truth

5.meaning: A sinner; one steeped in sin and wrongdoing. An emphatic form denoting someone given over to guilt and transgression.
5.grammar: A masculine adjective/noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) ('deeply, habitually sinful'). The final -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a sinner') and in the genitive case, the form used after a preceding noun or a preposition.
5.root: أ-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — to sin, do wrong; guilt

1.meaning: They pass on / they convey — third-person masculine plural present of 'to cast, to throw, to transmit'; describing how devils relay overheard information.

parts.en: they cast / pass on (Form IV muḍāriʿ 3rd masculine plural)

1.grammar: Form IV muḍāriʿ third-person masculine plural (-ūna indicative). The Form IV of l-q-y conveys throwing something toward someone, including passing on information.
1.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet; Form IV: to throw toward, to cast, to deliver

2.meaning: The hearing — the faculty or sense of hearing, the capacity by which sound is perceived, made definite by 'the.'
2.grammar: A noun with the prefix al- ('the'); its l assimilates into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced as-samʿ. The final -a marks the accusative, the case for the object of a verb. It denotes the sense of hearing as a definite, known thing.

3.meaning: 'And most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger number among a group of people. 'akthar' is the comparative/superlative 'more / most'.
3.grammar: Joined by 'wa' ('and'). 'akthar' is an elative ('more/most, the greater part') on the pattern 'afʿal'. The '-u' ending is nominative, generally marking the word as a subject. The attached '-hum' means 'of them / their' (a group of males), so the whole means 'and most of them'.
3.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

4.meaning: Liars / those who tell falsehoods — the definite plural active participle of 'to lie', in the nominative; a predicate describing a group as deceivers.

parts.en: liars (Form I active participle, masculine plural nominative)

4.grammar: The -ūna ending is masculine sound plural nominative. kādhibūna is the Form I active participle of k-dh-b, meaning 'those who lie'. Predicate of a nominal sentence.

1.meaning: And the poets — conjunction plus the definite plural of shāʿir (poet, one who perceives deeply); in context, a dismissive label applied to the Prophet by his opponents.
1.grammar: The wa- is conjunctive. al-shuʿarāu is the broken plural of shāʿir (poet), nominative (the -u ending). The definite article makes them a specific category.
1.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to feel, to perceive; a poet (one who deeply feels/perceives)

2.meaning: Follow them / pursue them — third-person masculine plural present of 'to follow', with a third-person masculine plural object pronoun; describing who follows the poets.
2.grammar: Form VIII muḍāriʿ (deliberate following) third-person masculine singular (the plural subject comes after). The suffix -humu is the third-person masculine plural object 'them'; the -u is a helping vowel.
2.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to adhere to

3.meaning: The deviators / those who go astray — the definite plural active participle of 'to deviate'; those who wander from truth and follow whims.

parts.en: the deviators (active participle, masculine plural nominative)

3.grammar: The -ūna ending is masculine sound plural nominative. al-ghāwūna is the Form I active participle of gh-w-y: those who go astray or are led by vain desires.
3.root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y) — to go astray, to deviate, to follow passion

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You see, perceive, or take notice; to observe with the eye, or by extension to come to know or consider. Often used to draw attention, as in 'have you considered…?'
2.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single male 'you,' marked by the 'ta-' prefix. The root's weak final letter has dropped, leaving the short final -a; this shortened form is the jussive/apocopated form, which appears after certain particles (such as 'did not' or in questions like 'have you not seen?').
2.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider, form an opinion

3.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
3.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
5.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
5.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

6.meaning: A valley / a wadi — a dry riverbed or valley; used figuratively for roaming aimlessly in the wastelands of imagination.
6.grammar: The -in ending (without nunation on the final ī, as it is a defective noun) marks indefinite genitive. wādī refers to a valley or watercourse, often dry except in rain season.
6.root: و-د-ي (w-d-y) — valley, wadi; to flow (as in a watercourse)

7.meaning: They roam / they wander aimlessly — third-person masculine plural present of 'to wander distractedly'; describing the aimless wandering of poets in flights of fancy.

parts.en: they wander aimlessly (Form I muḍāriʿ 3rd masculine plural)

7.grammar: Form I muḍāriʿ third-person masculine plural (-ūna indicative). The root h-y-m conveys passionate, distracted wandering — like a lovesick camel or someone lost in fantasy.
7.root: ه-ي-م (h-y-m) — to wander distractedly, to be madly passionate, to roam aimlessly

1.meaning: 'And that they…' — the connector 'wa-' ('and') joined to 'anna' ('that, indeed') and the pronoun 'they,' introducing a further affirmed clause.
1.grammar: Begins with 'wa-' ('and'). Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a clause and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

2.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: They do / they were doing — a verb of general doing or acting, performing a deed.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the basic Form I. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb is the general one for doing, making, or carrying out an action.
5.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, performing an act

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: And they remembered / and they mention — conjunction plus third-person masculine plural perfect of 'to remember or mention Allah'; a positive exception describing the righteous among poets.

parts.en: they remembered / mentioned (Form I perfect 3rd masculine plural)

6.grammar: The wa- is conjunctive (here in the exception clause). dhakarū is Form I perfect third-person masculine plural; the wāw marks the plural.
6.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
7.root: — (proper name)

8.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
8.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
8.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

9.meaning: And they defend themselves / and they take revenge for themselves — conjunction plus Form VIII third-person masculine plural perfect of 'to seek victory for oneself'; the righteous defending against oppressors.

parts.en: they defended themselves / took revenge (Form VIII perfect 3rd masculine plural)

9.grammar: The wa- is conjunctive. intaṣarū is Form VIII perfect third-person masculine plural of n-ṣ-r (reflexive: 'sought victory for themselves'). The wāw marks the plural.
9.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help; Form VIII: to defend oneself, to seek victory for oneself

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
11.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
11.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: A third-person plural past-tense passive verb meaning 'they were wronged / treated unjustly / oppressed.' It marks people as the recipients of injustice done to them.
13.grammar: Past-tense passive verb (the internal vowel pattern u-i signals 'the action was done to them, not by them'). The '-ū' ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural), here the ones to whom the wrong was done.
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression, putting something out of its rightful place

14.meaning: "and he will surely come to know" — the conjunction "and" with a marker of certain futurity attached to a verb meaning "to know," conveying that knowledge will definitely come to a single male subject in time.
14.grammar: Built from wa- ("and") plus the future prefix sa- ("will," indicating an action yet to come). The ya- prefix marks the subject as "he," and the -u ending is the indicative present marker. Together the prefixes turn "he knows" into "he will know."

15.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
15.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

16.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
16.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

17.meaning: Which / what — an interrogative pronoun in the accusative (governed by a following verb or preposition); asking about 'which' or 'what' turning point.
17.grammar: ayya is the accusative form of the interrogative pronoun ayy (which/what). The -a ending marks the accusative.

18.meaning: A turning point / a place of return — the verbal noun of 'to return or be overturned'; refers to where one will end up, the final destination or reversal.

parts.en: a place of return / a turning point (indefinite genitive)

18.grammar: The -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks indefinite genitive. munqalab is the Form VII verbal noun (mif'al pattern) of q-l-b: a place or act of turning/returning.
18.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn; a place of turning, a reversal

19.meaning: They will return / they will be turned back — third-person masculine plural present of the Form VII verb 'to be overturned or returned'; referring to where wrongdoers will end up.

parts.en: they return / will be turned back (Form VII muḍāriʿ 3rd masculine plural)

19.grammar: Form VII muḍāriʿ (reflexive: to be turned, to return) third-person masculine plural (-ūna indicative). The initial n- of Form VII assimilates into the ya- prefix.
19.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; Form VII: to be turned back, to return
